premises: A pile of monthly receipts for a rented booking page grows each month until you build your own and the pile stops.

One barber shop's booking app, Juno Cuts, grows from one sentence: a calendar, hours that bounce a Sunday request, Sam's confirmation email, a $20 Stripe deposit, then it goes live on junocuts.com, where Sam books and pays.
A shop's paper appointment book is turned into a website page by page, each page a feature the Agent adds.
story.why: One shop and one client make every feature a visible change to the same app: the viewer watches Sam's Friday 3 PM slot get booked, confirmed, paid for and finally booked on the shop's own domain, which keeps the hook's promise.
story.spine: You rent a booking page every month. But one sentence builds your own booking app. Therefore it bounces a Sunday request and emails Sam's confirmation. But an unpaid booking is a no-show, so one more prompt adds a Stripe deposit. Therefore it goes live on junocuts.com, until Sam books and pays on your own page.
story.ending: Sam's phone shows junocuts.com with Fri 3 PM booked and $20 paid: SAM PAID, FRI 3 PM BOOKED.
